cards.explanation: The answer is all his life. The writer says, "I will praise the LORD all my life; I will sing praises to my God while I have my being." (Psalm 146:2) He's saying what he plans to do, and he doesn't hang any conditions on it. I wish I could make promises that big, friends, because I once swore I'd only eat ONE broken cookie per batch.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "Put not your trust in princes, in mortal man, who cannot save." (Psalm 146:3) Princes are impressive, friends, but the psalm calls them mortal men. Trust placed there has nothing to hold it up.

The answer is False. The psalm says his plans perish "on that very day…" (Psalm 146:4) When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground, and his plans perish the same day. A prince can have the biggest plans in the kingdom, and the psalm still says they perish.

The answer is in the LORD his God. "Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God…" (Psalm 146:5) Help and hope land in the same place, friends. The God of Jacob is the God who spoke to Jacob, whom God also named Israel (Genesis 35:10).

The answer is False. The psalm says, "He remains faithful forever." (Psalm 146:6) It doesn't say "as long as," and it doesn't hang His faithfulness on anyone else. Compare that to the man in verse 4, whose plans perish the day his spirit departs.

The answer is that He executes justice for them. "He executes justice for the oppressed…" (Psalm 146:7) It's the first thing named in the list, bakers, and the very next line is food for the hungry. The oppressed are the ones this verse says He brings justice to.

The answer is prisoners. "The LORD sets the prisoners free…" (Psalm 146:7) It comes right after the food for the hungry. That line gets me every single time, friends. Somebody locked up, and the LORD is the One opening the door.

The answer is the righteous. "…the LORD loves the righteous." (Psalm 146:8) That line sits right after He opens the eyes of the blind and lifts those weighed down, bakers. It's all one long list of what He does.

The answer is that He frustrates them. The psalm says, "…but the ways of the wicked He frustrates." (Psalm 146:9) Everything before it in the verse was about the LORD caring for foreigners, the fatherless and the widow, friends. Then comes the turn.
The answer is forever. "The LORD reigns forever, your God, O Zion, for all generations." (Psalm 146:10) Forever, and for all generations, bakers. Princes come and go, but this reign doesn't end.
